title: Qt: Concurrently fill display filter expression dialog
description:
Use QtConcurrent to create and sort widget items. The dialog window is
immediately visible and usable. Search becomes available once all items
are added to the tree.

When compiled with Qt5, all items are added in bulk. Qt6 features new
QPromise interface that makes it possible to add tree items one by one.

notes.body: changed title from **Qt: {-Do not spin event loops in-} display filter dialog** to **Qt: {+Concurrently fill+} display filter {+expression +}dialog**
Should we consider moving this dialog away from QTreeWidget to a QTreeView? Seems to me we are doing a lot of "special changes" just to accommodate to the QTreeWidget shortcomings.

I don't think the migration to `QTreeView` is worth is. The code would still have to fetch and sort protocol fields. If sorting was carried by underlying API (i.e. proto_get_first_protocol()/proto_get_next_protocol() and proto_get_first_protocol_field()/proto_get_next_protocol_field() could return alphabetically sorted list) then maybe implementing `QTreeView` would make some sense (but more to reduce memory usage rather than speed things up), but I don't have any high hopes regarding it.

The thing is, we would not implement the sorting, nor the filtering as we could use the proxy models for that and just focus on stuff like "lessThan" or "filterAcceptsRow". It just enhances the capabilities greatly on what you can do.

Also, although QTreeWidget uses QTreeView underneath, they need to do conversions every few steps, making the system a lot slower than if it would be implemented as pure Model/View. And handling "protocol_get_first/next_protocol" is just built-in.

I get why you don't want to do it with this change and I am totally ok with it. Its on my list for conversion anyway so I will do it sometime in the near future.

commits_data.title: Qt: Do not spin event loops in display filter dialog
commits_data.message:
Qt: Do not spin event loops in display filter dialog

Pass comparator function so the list gets sorted alphabetically. Without
the comparator function, the pointer values were sorted. Insert already
sorted data into tree widget and thus remove the redundant sort call.

Use std::stable_sort() instead of std::sort() as stable sort is actually
faster here. The std::stable_sort() tends to do fewer comparisons and
more moves than std::sort(). When sorting QTreeWidgetItem pointers, the
move is very low cost (only the pointer itself is moved) and string
comparison is quite heavy (especially because the strings share common
prefix).
